statement: The function returns a successful result r. Let ys be the sequence of values in r, and let cnt(xs, v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(xs) and xs[i] = v. Then ys is exactly the subsequence of xs obtained by keeping every position i for which cnt(xs, xs[i]) = 1 and deleting every position i for which cnt(xs, xs[i]) >= 2, with all kept positions remaining in their original relative order. Equivalently, for every value v, cnt(ys, v) = 1 if cnt(xs, v) = 1, and cnt(ys, v) = 0 otherwise, and ys is a subsequence of xs in the order inherited from xs.
preconditions: Let xs be the sequence of values in head from front to back. The list is finite and nonempty: 1 <= len(xs) <= 100000. Every node value lies in the constraint range: for every i with 0 <= i < len(xs), 1 <= xs[i] <= 100000.
